historical_measurement_sources.method: git show COMMIT:benchmarks/runtime/PATH; SHA256 of blob bytes

interpretation.breadth_goal: 80% is a qualitative design aspiration for representative everyday-codebase breadth; no population percentage or CPU-time coverage is measured.
interpretation.classification: A paired 95% bootstrap interval wholly below 1 is faster than Go, wholly above 1 is slower, and containing 1 is overlapping. This is descriptive evidence, not an equivalence proof or acceptance threshold; multiple comparisons are not adjusted.
interpretation.counts_scope: Counts describe these selected test/profile comparisons only, not percentages of real codebases or operation frequencies.
interpretation.taxonomy_review: Assess each operation family and composed application separately. Matching performance across these workloads supports confidence for applications with similar operations, input shapes, working sets and lifetimes. Do not infer a percentage of real codebases from case counts or CPU samples, and do not let one library win offset unrelated weaknesses.
confidence_gaps: large working sets and cache-miss-heavy access
map deletion, high-cardinality and varied-length keys
varied text, numeric and structured-data shapes
concurrency, synchronization, asynchronous scheduling and I/O
notes: alloc_short permits optimizer elimination of nonescaping allocations; fastest saved pilots are exceptionally short. It is not evidence for the cost of physical allocation.
sort_int/sort_records use each language native sorting API and compare language/library policies, rather than one identical algorithm.
Ownership, snapshot, copy-on-write, reference-counting, GC and allocator semantics differ as documented; equivalent observable behavior does not imply equivalent physical copying.
Optimized default build policies use different instruction sets across arms. Rust default x86_64 and Go v1 differ from default Zig/Clang-derived host features.
Paired intervals and raw spread describe the saved run. They do not guarantee performance on another machine, input, lifetime or workload.

target_policy.my-llvm: default Zig/Clang-derived CPU/features; first target CPU and merged target features
target_policy.policy_note: Optimized default build policies; instruction sets are not matched across arms. No forced target tuning or disabled MyLang checks.
target_policy.rust_text: cargo release defaults, portable target; locked serde_json dependency
target_policy.mylang_symbols: --keep-symbols preserves names for profiling; release optimization remains enabled
